report_meta.entity_quote: System and Organization Controls 2 (SOC 2) Type 2 Report on controls placed in operation at Deepgram, Inc.
report_meta.auditor_quote: CyberGuard Compliance, LLP Las Vegas, NV February 27, 2026
report_meta.period_quote: relevant to security, availability, and confidentiality ... For the Period January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025

3.1.1.quote: The Company uses Transport Layer Security (TLS 1.2 or higher) for transmitting sensitive data over public networks.
3.1.1.note: Control 6.6.5, tested with no exceptions noted. Report says '1.2 or higher'; TLS 1.2 is the stated minimum.

3.1.2.quote: Encryption is used to protect data used, transmitted, and stored. Trusted keys and/or certificates are used in order to establish validation.
3.1.2.note: At-rest encryption affirmed; no cipher standard (AES etc.) named anywhere in the report.

3.1.3.quote: Confidential data files are encrypted prior to backup.
3.1.3.note: Control 6.1.14, tested with no exceptions noted; standard not specified.

3.1.4.quote: Secure keys are managed by a Key Management System. ... Key management is in place to support cryptographic techniques established by the Company.
3.1.4.note: Second sentence is control 6.1.8, p56. Deepgram-managed KMS is stated, but the report never says whether keys are customer-specific — confirm with vendor before locking the dropdown.

3.1.8.value:
Multi-factor authentication enforced on production network domain, in-scope applications, and database
Firewalls restrict unnecessary ports/protocols/services; IDS/IPS continuously monitors network traffic
Administrative access only via encrypted VPN tunnel
Internal and external vulnerability scans quarterly; penetration tests of key systems at least annually
Centralized, access-restricted log storage to support forensics
Comprehensive Incident Response Plan with annual training and tabletop exercises
3.1.8.quote: The production network domain is configured to enforce the following password requirements: Minimum Password Length, Multi-Factor Authentication

3.2.1.value: No country or EU statement in the report. Hosted solution runs in colocation data centers (geographically disparate); AWS and Azure are carved-out subservice organizations used as backup/recovery providers.
3.2.1.quote: The hosted solution runs on a colo-infrastructure operating out of colocation data centers. AWS and Azure are leveraged for recovery and non-critical elements of the system.
3.2.1.note: p22: data center levels are 'geographically disparate in order to withstand region-wide failures'. p26 lists CSOC carve-outs: Colocation Data Centers, AWS, Microsoft Azure.

absent: 3.1.6 anonymization — not addressed anywhere in report
3.1.7 pseudonymization — not addressed anywhere in report
3.2.1 EU Access / data residency — no country, region, or EU statement anywhere in report
At-rest and backup encryption cipher standard (AES etc.) — never specified
Customer-specificity of encryption keys — not stated (see 3.1.4 note)
